#800. IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos

An enormous number of invisible particles are constantly traveling through Earth, passing through our bodies and continuing into space as though almost nothing stands in their way. Known as neutrinos, these mysterious particles are among the most difficult objects in the universe to detect. Yet scientists are finding ways to capture evidence of their passage, opening new opportunities to investigate the cosmos and its most extreme environments.

Neutrino research has played a remarkable role in modern physics. Discoveries involving these particles have contributed to five Nobel Prizes in Physics. This year, physicist Francis Halzen received the prestigious award "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin."

George Fuller, a Distinguished Professor of Physics at the University of California San Diego, has studied nuclear physics, particle astrophysics, and cosmology for decades. He also collaborated with Halzen on an early scientific paper about IceCube. His expertise helps explain what makes neutrinos so unusual and why scientists built an enormous observatory deep within the Antarctic ice to study them.

Neutrinos belong to a group known as elementary particles, which scientists believe have no smaller components. They come in three varieties, called electron, muon, and tau neutrinos. Unlike electrically charged particles, neutrinos have no electric charge. They do have mass, but it is extraordinarily small, potentially around 10 million times less than the mass of an electron. Their exact masses remain unknown, as does the mechanism responsible for producing them.

Another remarkable characteristic is their ability to travel through matter with almost no resistance. Because neutrinos interact so rarely with other particles, they can cross vast distances at speeds approaching the speed of light.

Neutrinos originate from many different places, including the Sun, distant regions of space, and sources scientists have yet to identify. They are also astonishingly abundant. Estimates suggest the universe contains roughly 1089 neutrinos, equivalent to approximately one billion for every atom in existence.

"Neutrinos are truly ghost-like particles," stated Fuller. "It's hard to stop them. It's hard to catch them. How do we even know they exist or where they are?"

Ghost Particles That Pass Through Almost Anything

Despite their elusive nature, neutrinos occasionally interact with matter through a fundamental force known as the weak interaction. This force is approximately 20 orders of magnitude weaker than electromagnetism. Such interactions can cause neutrinos to scatter or be absorbed, providing scientists with a way to detect them. However, these events are so uncommon that observing them requires exceptionally sensitive equipment.

Their ability to move through dense material also makes neutrinos valuable messengers from otherwise inaccessible regions of the universe. They can escape from environments surrounding collapsing stars and black holes, carrying information that other forms of radiation might not reveal.

The scale of this invisible activity is staggering. Approximately 100 billion neutrinos pass through every square centimeter of your body each second, almost entirely unnoticed.

"Because the interaction is so weak, neutrinos can get through almost anything," said Fuller. "Light years of lead -- depending on their energy, they would go right through it."

How Scientists Learned to Detect Neutrinos

The search for neutrinos began long before technology existed to observe them. During the 1930s, physicist Wolfgang Pauli proposed that an unknown particle might explain why energy appeared to be missing during certain forms of radioactive decay. He initially used a different name for the hypothetical particle (he called them "neutrons" at the time).

Pauli understood how difficult it would be to verify his idea. He famously acknowledged the problem by saying, "I have done a terrible thing, I have postulated a particle that cannot be detected."

For decades, neutrinos remained beyond the reach of experiments. That changed in 1956, when physicists Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines successfully detected them in an experiment known as "Project Poltergeist."

The breakthrough established that neutrinos were real, but detecting them remained an enormous challenge. Scientists needed increasingly sophisticated instruments to investigate the rarest and most energetic neutrinos arriving from space.

Why Antarctica Is Ideal for Hunting Cosmic Neutrinos

During the 1990s, Halzen recognized that the South Pole offered an extraordinary natural environment for neutrino research. Far below Antarctica's surface, immense volumes of ice are exceptionally clear, with relatively few bubbles or contaminants to interfere with the detection of faint flashes of light.

His vision eventually led to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory, a gigantic scientific instrument embedded within roughly one cubic kilometer of Antarctic ice. To construct it, researchers drilled deep holes and lowered long strings of sensitive light detectors called photomultiplier tubes.

These instruments search for brief flashes of blue light produced through a phenomenon called Cherenkov radiation. The light appears when a neutrino interacts with matter in the ice and produces a charged particle traveling faster than light can move through that material.

By recording these flashes, researchers can identify evidence of neutrinos that would otherwise pass through Earth without leaving a detectable trace.

IceCube is particularly important for studying neutrinos that arrive from distant cosmic sources with extraordinarily high energies. Unlike the enormous quantities of relatively low-energy neutrinos produced by the Sun, these powerful cosmic visitors are extremely rare. The observatory detects only a few dozen of the most energetic examples each year.

When one of these neutrinos interacts with the ice, it can produce a rapidly moving electron or muon. A muon, for example, generates a cone of Cherenkov light as it travels through the ice. Scientists analyze the resulting pattern of light to estimate the neutrino's energy and reconstruct the direction from which it arrived.

For Fuller, these exceptionally energetic neutrinos are among IceCube's most exciting discoveries because their origins and the physical processes responsible for accelerating them remain poorly understood.

"Some ultra-high-energy neutrinos detected at IceCube have roughly 10 billion times the energy of a typical neutrino from the Sun. One detected by a similar experiment has an energy 200 times higher than that. We don't really know where that neutrino came from," he stated. "The fact that it got here at all may be saying something profound about the universe. In that sense, Halzen really is at the frontier of experimental fundamental particle physics."

Neutrinos Could Reveal Secrets of the Big Bang

The scientific effort to understand neutrinos extends far beyond Antarctica. Researchers at UC San Diego are also involved in another major observatory that could offer new insights into these elusive particles and the universe's earliest history.

Located high in Chile's Atacama Desert, the Simons Observatory is gathering information about the cosmic microwave background, the ancient radiation left over from the early universe. Often described as the oldest light in the cosmos, this radiation provides a valuable record of conditions that existed shortly after the Big Bang.

UC San Diego helped establish the observatory, and Brian Keating, a Distinguished Professor of Physics at the university, serves as its principal investigator.

Although the observatory primarily studies ancient light, its measurements can also reveal information about neutrinos from the earliest stages of cosmic history. The project could provide an enormous amount of new data related to these ancient particles, potentially offering insights that other experiments cannot obtain.

Fuller believes the anticipated observations could improve scientists' understanding of the Big Bang, the early evolution of the universe, and other fundamental questions about how the cosmos developed.

"Halzen's work, and the work of those he inspired with his vision, was foundational in giving humanity a new window on the universe and on the mysterious and notoriously slippery neutrino," he stated.

Materials provided by University of California - San Diego. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#799. McTominay reveals heart treatment at World Cup

McTominay reveals he underwent heart procedure days before World Cup game

Scott McTominay says he received treatment to correct an irregular heartbeat two days before Scotland's World Cup win over Haiti in June.

The Napoli midfielder recently underwent an ablation procedure - a minimally invasive operation to correct irregular heart rhythms - in Manchester.

At the World Cup, the 29-year-old was was put to sleep to correct his heartbeat and given the all-clear to play in the opening 1-0 victory over Haiti in Massachusetts.

"I had to go and get the shock on my heart," revealed the former Manchester United player, who also played 90 minutes in the losses to Morocco and Brazil.

"It was two days before the Haiti game. You've prepared so well. I was in such good condition and then something like that happens. You're thinking, 'how is this happening to me?'

"You have to get on with it, that's the cards that you're dealt in football. Sometimes, things don't go your way.

"I was 100% [fit], but obviously, whenever you're sat in a hospital bed two days before the first game of the World Cup about to get put to sleep, it's not ideal, is it?"

McTominay praised his club and the medical staff who treated him in the autumn.

He missed Scotland's opening four Nations League fixtures - a win, a draw and two defeats - but has been recalled to the squad after returning to domestic and Champions League action with Napoli.

Sebastien Pocognoli's side host North Macedonia on Friday and visit Switzerland on Monday.

"Yeah, I'm good," said McTominay. "I'm feeling much, much better than what I was. I feel like it was something that needed to be done. In your career, you have moments like that where things can take you a bit by surprise.

"Obviously, it looks a lot worse to people in the media and family and friends who reach out to you after they see news related to a heart issue, but it's a relatively straightforward procedure, which went really, really well in Manchester.

"So just really happy to be back and playing football again. That's the most important thing in my life and it always will be in terms of wanting to come back and prove myself again and making sure that I can go to another level."

Nations League: Scotland v North Macedonia

McTominay added: "For me, it's always about coming back stronger.

"No matter how well you play in one game, it's about the next game and pushing yourself and recovering well and eating the right things, sleeping correctly throughout your career."

#798. Pochettino, Howe, Emery... or Carrick? Man Utd's managerial options

Eddie Howe, Mauricio Pochettino and Unai Emery have all been linked with replacing Michael Carrick as Manchester United boss

With one victory in their first 10 Premier League matches, Manchester United have made their worst start to a top-flight campaign since the 1986-87 season.

They are 18th in the table, one point above bottom club Crystal Palace.

United directors will meet in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Michael Carrick's future as his 10-month spell as head coach comes under major scrutiny.

If the 45-year-old former player departs, it would mean an eighth permanent boss for the Red Devils since Sir Alex Ferguson retired 13 years ago.

That would be as many managerial changes as they have made across the previous 68 years dating back to Sir Matt Busby's appointment in 1945.

BBC Sport takes a look at the leading candidates who could replace Carrick.

Mauricio Pochettino penned a new deal with with the USA in the summer

Major trophies won: 1 Ligue 1, 1 French Cup

Premier League record: P294, W150; Win percentage: 51; Points per game ratio (PPG): 1.77

Did you know: Pochettino averaged 1.89 points per game during his spell at Tottenham, the best ratio of any Spurs manager to have taken charge of 25 or more Premier League games.

United's long-standing interest in the Argentine, 54, dates back a decade.

At Spurs, he moulded their best team in a generation, but ultimately came up short of winning a trophy, losing both the Champions League and League Cup finals, and posted second and third-placed finishes. Silverware did come at Paris St-Germain with a league title, but a spell at Chelsea proved tougher with a League Cup final defeat by Liverpool in 2024.

Having led the USA to the last 16 of the World Cup on home soil he signed a new contract taking him up to the 2030 tournament. Pochettino has an exciting group of young players to work with for the national team - led by Manchester City-bound 17-year-old Cavan Sullivan - but he has always made it clear he has unfinished business in the Premier League.

A reported buyout clause in Pochettino's contract is worth $10million (Â£7.44m), while it is also understood to contain clauses that would allow him to leave for specific high-profile jobs.

Carrick's Man Utd future to be decided at Wednesday meeting

What Howe could bring to Man Utd - and what are the challenges?

Julian Nagelsmann resigned in the summer after Germany lost to Paraguay on penalties in the World Cup

Did you know: Only Hansi Flick (88.9%) has a better win percentage by a Bayern Munich manager in the Champions League than Nagelsmann's 83.3%.

Nagelsmann first impressed with his work at Hoffenheim, where he became the youngest head coach in Bundesliga history aged 28, leading them from relegation struggles to the Champions League.

He followed that by taking RB Leipzig to a Champions League semi-final in 2020 and Bayern Munich understandably came calling.

But despite winning the Bundesliga title in his first season he reportedly fell out with key players and did not survive a full second season.

In 2023, Nagelsmann took charge of a Germany side in transition, and they were narrowly beaten in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 by eventual winners Spain, but stepped down in the summer after Die Mannschaft were humbled by Paraguay in the World Cup last 32.

Still only 39, his reputation may have taken a bit of a hit, but the German is still regarded as one of Europe's best coaches. Manchester United's director of recruitment Christopher Vivell also knows him well, having worked together at RB Leipzig.

Eddie Howe oversaw more Premier League wins (84) than any other Newcastle manager

Premier League record: P369 W140; Win percentage: 37.9; PPG: 1.36

Did you know: Eddie Howe (five) is one of only three managers with five or more wins against Mikel Arteta in all competitions, along with Pep Guardiola (11) and Jurgen Klopp (six).

His body of work in English football needs little introduction having led Bournemouth to the top flight for the first time in their history, before he confirmed his place in Newcastle folklore with their first major domestic trophy since lifting the FA Cup in 1955.

The League Cup final triumph over Liverpool was one of the greatest days in the club's history, while he also secured two top-five finishes to take the club back into the Champions League for the first time in 20 years.

Howe, 48, left in the summer after an underwhelming 12th-placed finish last term and Newcastle would only be due a a relatively small amount of compensation should he be tempted by the Old Trafford job.

Antonio Conte called Tottenham's players "selfish" when he left after 16 months in 2023

Major trophies won: 5 Serie A, 1 Premier League, 1 FA Cup

Premier League record: P132, W83; Win percentage: 62.9; PPG: 2.03

Did you know: Chelsea won 30 of their 38 Premier League matches as they claimed the title in Antonio Conte's first season in charge in 2016-17.

A serial winner, Conte's managerial credentials are not in doubt.

He left Napoli of his own accord this summer just 12 months after delivering only the fourth top-flight title in their history.

That added to Serie A triumphs at Juventus (three) and Inter Milan, and spells at Chelsea and Tottenham.

Conte, 57, would appear to be a no-brainer of a choice to take over at United, but could the Italian's fiery nature and history of falling out with clubs count against him?

His last stint in English football ended under a cloud of controversy as he left Tottenham in 2023 following criticism of the players and the club's culture.

While he had success at Chelsea, Conte also reportedly clashed with both players and the board.

Emery has also managed Arsenal and Paris St-Germain in his career

Major trophies won: 5 Europa League, 1 Ligue 1, 2 French Cups, 2 French League Cups

Premier League record: P200, W101; Win percentage: 50.5; PPG: 1.75

Did you know: Unai Emery has the best Premier League win percentage (51%) and points per game ratio (1.75) of any permanent Aston Villa boss.

Vastly experienced, the Spaniard's stock is at an all-time high courtesy of the superb job he has done since taking over at Villa in October 2022.

Having taken the club into the European Cup/Champions League for the first time for 41 years, the 55-year-old then ended their 30-year wait for silverware with success in last season's Europa League.

Despite having lost the spine of his team over the summer, Emery's new-look side are finding their feet again and the chances of him leaving for United look even slimmer with recent news he is expected to sign a new contract.

Michael Carrick's Manchester United side have managed one win in 10 league games this season

Premier League record: P29, W14; Win percentage: 48.3; PPG: 1.76

Did you know: After his initial appointment as United's interim boss in January, Michael Carrick had the most wins (12) and points (39) of any Premier League manager during the rest of the 2025-26 season.

Still clinging on to his job in the Old Trafford hot seat, could United's hierarchy actually decide to keep faith with Carrick?

After such a brilliant start and end to the season following his arrival in January, the wheels have come off spectacularly this term with only three wins from 15 matches in all competitions.

His team have at least shown fight with comebacks in recent games to beat Roma and salvage a point in a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, but their overall stats are damning and the outlook doesn't look good for the 45-year-old, who won five Premier League titles and the Champions League as a United player.

The club are in the relegation zone and 18th is their lowest position after 10 games of a season for 40 years. It is also only the second time they have gone eight Premier League games without a victory.

#797. The Monaco summit that will decide the future of Carrick and Man Utd

Manchester United minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left), chief executive Omar Berrada (centre) and director of football Jason Wilcox will decide Michael Carrick's fate as head coach

Michael Carrick's future as Manchester United head coach will be determined 800 miles away from Old Trafford in Monaco on Wednesday.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are flying out for one of their regular pre-planned meetings to discuss strategy around the football club.

On this occasion, the main issue to be decided is Carrick's future and what should happen next.

It is expected that Berrada and Wilcox's recommendation is for the head coach to go.

It is not a situation Sir Jim Ratcliffe can have expected to find himself in again, less than three years after purchasing a minority stake in United.

On Christmas Eve 2023, his vision was much different.

"Our shared ambition is clear: we all want to see Manchester United back where we belong, at the very top of English, European and world football," he said.

Instead, United are 18th, in the Premier League's relegation zone after winning just one of their first 10 games and none since August. It is their lowest position so far into a top-flight season since 1986-87 when they were 20th.

Ratcliffe has been criticised for many decisions since he bought his 28.94% stake for just over Â£1bn. This is one he really needs to get right.

Ratcliffe's home is in Monaco and his company Ineos has offices in the principality.

The meeting had been in the diary for some time as a regular catch-up between senior executives and their boss.

Sources have stressed that the choice of location was not influenced by the debate around Carrick's future - it just happens to now be the most important item for discussion.

The decision to sack United's previous two managers was not made in a meeting in Monaco.

Ruben Amorim was sacked 19 hours after his explosive media conference following a 1-1 draw at Leeds in January.

Erik ten Hag went a day after Manchester United lost at West Ham leaving them with just three wins from their opening nine matches

A decision to sack Dutchman Ten Hag was taken at a meeting of senior Ineos executives in the summer of 2024, only for the choice to be reversed following the FA Cup final triumph over Manchester City.

Four months later there was a six-hour meeting at Ineos HQ in London as Ten Hag's tenure hung by a thread. He survived again but was gone three weeks later.

Amorim was summoned to Monaco after the Europa League final defeat to Tottenham in 2025.

There is daily contact between senior executives so if the meeting was purely to decide Carrick's fate, it could be done by video conference and the need to travel to Monaco is not the reason why there is yet to be a decision.

The travel element does add a complication given the preference for Berrada and Wilcox is to inform Carrick of any decision face to face.

Sources say the Monaco meetings used to be held every six weeks, although in more recent times they are less frequent.

Those who have attended them say they take place in the morning, tend to last between three and four hours and usually stop on time so Ratcliffe can go for his regular lunchtime jog.

Pochettino, Howe, Emery... or Carrick? Man Utd's managerial options

What Howe could bring to Man Utd - and what are the challenges?

Carrick won 12 games out of 17 as interim boss to earn a two-year contract as Manchester United head coach in the summer

United stood by Carrick after the woeful 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October.

Club sources were adamant they wanted to give Carrick and his players a chance to turn the situation around it was also felt that the two-week international break in November represented a better chance for the club to properly assess the club's start to the campaign.

However, although they did end a long wait for a victory against Roma on 3 November, United had to come from two goals down to seal a 3-2 victory in a chaotic game.

They failed to press home their advantage after excelling in the first half against Chelsea and eventually lost 2-0 as experienced central defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off.

On Sunday, they conceded twice inside five minutes and had to come from two goals down twice to claim a point against Villa.

While sources said the comebacks showed the United squad were still playing for Carrick, it is also understood the chaotic nature of the games and the inability to stop the opposition from scoring has led Berrada and Wilcox, who were at all three matches, to conclude a change of coach is required to get United out of the mess they find themselves in.

United have conceded 30 goals so far this season in 15 games - 19 in 10 Premier League matches, eight in four in the Champions League and three in their one Carabao Cup tie.

Instead of replacing Carrick another option under consideration is additional coaching support to assist the current team.

Bayern Munich coach Aaron Danks, who worked with Carrick at Middlesbrough and was touted as a potential appointment in the summer, is one option.

Manchester United co-chair Avram Glazer (left) with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe at the 2025 Europa League final

If Ratcliffe was to decide otherwise, it would raise serious questions over the future of Berrada and Wilcox.

How could they work with Carrick again in that scenario?

The pair have been the subject of intense and frequent fan discontent. But sources are adamant that Ratcliffe still retains faith in the pair, even though United are heading towards sacking a manager in mid-season for the third successive year, having backed them in the summer and spend millions on new players.

Ratcliffe is a ruthless operator, and has clear opinions of his own. He also has form, spending Â£5m hiring Dan Ashworth as sporting director from Newcastle in 2024, then waiting for the 55-year-old to spend five months on gardening leave before he could start work.

Five months later, Ashworth was sacked due to a divergence of opinion over who should replace Ten Hag. Ashworth felt someone with Premier League experience was a better fit for United's squad. Ratcliffe wanted a more modern alternative. Berrada suggested Amorim. Wilcox, after initial reservations, also got on board. Amorim was dismissed after 14 months.

The other unknown element is the Glazer family. They will need to sign off any decision.

At the time of the Ratcliffe purchase, United confirmed the club's 'board' had handed over responsibility for the football side. But United's articles of association state that responsibilities delegated by directors can also be "revoked or altered".

Crucially, of the 12 current directors, six are members of the Glazer family, including co-chairs Joel and Avi Glazer. United's rules state that if required, the chairman of any meeting will have a second and casting vote.

Although there have been media reports of Glazer dissatisfaction at United's current plight, there has been no public statement on the matter.

It may seem strange, but the reality is, as with any employee, Carrick will continue to do his job until told otherwise - and so far, there has been no conversation to that effect.

Although most of his squad, and a significant number of academy players, are on international duty, a core remains at home.

This includes Mason Mount, Joshua Zirkzee and Matthijs de Ligt. Harry Maguire, who suffered a back spasm against Villa, is also there, as are other injured players, including Luke Shaw and Marcus Rashford.

Carrick gave his players a day off on Monday but scheduled training days for Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. After that, they are not due to report back until 17 November, by which time the international contingent should start to return and begin preparations for the trip to Liverpool on 22 November.

"Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so, but as a normal international week is, we'll have some training and we'll have one or two days off," Carrick said after the Villa game. "Not too much. But we'll train and get ready for the next game."

Mauricio Pochettino was appointed USA boss in September 2024

If the discussions go as anticipated, replacing Carrick will be a key element.

Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as a leading contender and is known to be keen on the job.

United spoke to the former Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea boss about their managerial position on three different occasions - first of all when Jose Mourinho was sacked in 2018, then in 2022 when the club decided on Ten Hag instead and then again when the Dutchman was sacked.

The obvious problem is that Pochettino currently has a job as head coach of the United States. He renewed his contract in August and has a two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti over the next week. The Argentine, 54, is due to speak to the media on Friday and has a $10m (Â£7.5m) release clause.

Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe is out of work and available. BBC Sport has reported the compensation due to his old club if Manchester United appointed thr 48-year-old now would be Â£3m. But it reduces as the season goes on and would be nothing in the summer.

Italian Antonio Conte is also thought to be keen and the 57-year-old has Premier League title-winning experience at Chelsea and more recently won Serie A with Napoli last season, before leaving the club.

Julian Nagelsmann stood down as Germany boss in the wake of their last-32 exit at the World Cup exit at the World Cup but the German, 39, won the Bundesliga title with Bayern Munich in 2022-23.

Kieran McKenna was part of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's coaching team at Manchester United and left Ipswich after four-and-a-half years this summer. However, it is felt more likely United would want a candidate with greater experience than the 40-year-old Northern Irishman.

Where does this all leave Carrick? In a unenviable position of carrying on as if it was business as usual when the reality is anything but.

#796. How Kelly Clarkson Helps Daughter River Navigate "Hard" Junior High

The Voice’s Kelly Clarkson shared insight into parenting her daughter River Rose, 12, as she navigates school, friendships and conflict during an exclusive E! News interview: "Junior high sucks."

Kelly Clarkson's daughter is spreading her wings and learning to fly above the drama.

As her and late ex-husband Brandon Blackstock's 12-year-old daughter River Rose experiences the ups and downs of junior high school, the Voice coach shared how she took a chance, made a change and guided the tween to break away from the woes of adolescence. nice

"I'm a pretty progressive parent, so I'm like, 'No, no. You're gonna make your own mistakes, and that's OK,'" Clarkson told E! News' Will Marfuggi in an exclusive interview on The Voice season 30 live show red carpet on Nov. 9. "I'm not like an 'I told you so,' but I do implement advice."

"They're growing up," she continued. "One's in junior high, and junior high sucks. It's a hard age with friends, and arguing and stuff like that. I do offer advice, and I've had my daughter come back and be like, 'So you were right.'"

But the 44-year-old—also mom to 10-year-old son Remington Alexander with Blackstock—will always help her daughter stand a little taller, even when she doesn't heed her mom's warnings.

As she explained, "I've had them be like, 'OK, so I didn't do that, and I should have.'"

While Clarkson is hitting all the right notes of motherhood, she's also had a pitch-perfect time on The Voice alongside fellow coaches Adam Levine, Queen Latifah and Riley Green.

Although the Maroon 5 frontman took home gold last season with Alexia Jayy, he couldn't wait another minute to focus on this season.

"He doesn't really brag like that," Clarkson said. "He's not that guy. I totally would. I'd be like, 'Good luck,' just for fun or whatever. But he's pretty chill about it."

But the "Breakaway" singer would be lyin' if she said she wasn't looking forward to working with Latifah and Green as the newest additions experience the live rounds for the first time.

"What's amazing about Queen is she's such a legend," Clarson emphasized. "I know people throw around the term legend a lot, but she actually is. She's done so much, be it Broadway and movie musicals, be it rapping, be it singing, be it acting, whatever it is. She's just always doing stuff."

Simply put, "That brought just a legendary kind of status to the show for us this season."

Meanwhile, the "Worst Way" singer has definitely brought more than wine and roses to the singing competition.

"Riley is just currently crushing it on the charts, like everywhere," she continued. "His career is blown up. It's a different point in his career for him, too. So it's fun. They're bringing that different energy of what's happening in their world at this chapter in their lives."

While fans wait to see who wins big during The Voice season 30, press the red button and keep reading for surprising secrets about the series.

Does the winner of The Voice get any money?

The winner of The Voice is promised a recording contract with Universal Music Group, the monetary value of which is technically unknown.

But while NBC and series producers have never confirmed any amount, the last singer standing at the end of the competition reportedly gets $100,000.

Past winners have acknowledged getting paid, season 18 champ Todd Tilghman telling People in 2020, "I don't have any immediate plans to make any drastic changes tomorrow. I don't know for sure the direction my life will go in. There's a possibility that that money might pay the bills for a little while."

But, he added, since his wife had promised their kids a trip to Disney World, he guessed he'd be splurging on that too.

Not that the value of the music opportunities that open up for the winners should be discounted.

“I’ve got a catalog of songs. I have a lot of writer friends I want to collaborate with," season 27 winner Adam David of Team Bublé told Parade in May 2025. "The plan is to put out some music and go on to work. We’re going to put out some music, and we’re going to hit the road."

How does an aspiring contestant get to The Voice's Blind Auditions?

In addition to individual recruiting (such as when producers reached out to Frenchie Davis eight years after she was on American Idol), The Voice traditionally held in-person auditions around the U.S. Lately, however, the talent search is online, judges holding virtual open calls and weeding through video submissions to find singers who then may get a chance to sing for the coaches in hopes that at least one of them turns around.

Contestants must be at least 13 years old when they embark on their audition journey. The hopefuls have 90 seconds to introduce themselves and sing. They can sing anything they want but, per the show's FAQ page, they're encouraged to pick a tune "that best suits your voice and represents you as an artist."

Judges listen to auditions for "five or six days with approximately 18 to 20 auditions per day," executive producer Audrey Morrissey told SheKnows in 2018. Once they're selected for the blind round, she explained, "Artists are with us for several days prior to [their audition] to rehearse with our band, work with wardrobe/styling and camera block on the audition stage."

Then there's the filming to put together the packages introducing some of the hopefuls and their families, all of which came as a surprise to season six alum Ddendyl Hoyt. "I had no idea that reality TV was filmed kind of like a drama," she told the Washington Post in 2014, “So everything is filmed in segments and that’s kind of the longest process of it all.”

How many times can you audition for The Voice?

If at first you don't make it out of the untelevised rounds—or onto a team if you do make it to the blind auditions—you're free to try out as many times as you want, albeit only once per season.

"I can't be a mean judge," coach Reba McEntire, who won season 25 with Asher HaVon, told Newsweek in 2023. "It's good just to say, 'If you want to come back again, try it again next season, maybe a song that suits you, one that you're really comfortable with and that really shows your talent,' give them advice and encourage them to come back."

As of season 28, there's also the Carson Callback card to be played, in which longtime host Carson Daly grants an aspiring artist who didn't get any takers another shot.

Do The Voice contestants get to pick out their own clothing?

The show has a massive wardrobe department that ensures the contestants take the stage in elevated fashion—once they've made it onto a team.

"We shop for each artist to come up with great looks," Morrissey told SheKnows. "Once we get to the live shows, looks are customized for each specific performance."

How much time do the coaches really spend working with The Voice artists?

The celebrity coaches might not be pulling all-nighters, but they're invested in getting their teams ready for the battle rounds and beyond.

"The coaching sessions take place over four days," Morrissey said, "and the actual battle performances take two days."

Meanwhile, she added, how involved a coach gets with each artist "depends on the coach. Some love a big production and like working out all the details…Other coaches mainly focus on the music and arrangement for the performance."

Some coaches "are avid texters while others email," Morrissey added. "All off-camera interactions intensify as the artists move through the competition and the stakes get higher."

But it takes a village, former contestant Hoyt telling the Post, "What they don't show is all the coaching that comes from the staff: The vocal coaches, the band director, the producers, everyone has notes for you."

Snoop Dogg told Access Hollywood in September 2025, "The behind-the-scenes people don't get the credit that they deserve. It's a lot of people, moving things, making it happen…All of these people back here that make our job easy, all we gotta do is walk onstage and do what we do."

Who picks the songs the contestants sing on The Voice?

Between coaches and artists, Morrissey said, “The No. 1 communication is about song choice.”

The artists can theoretically offer their two cents when it comes to picking their songs, but usually the coaches rule on that front.

Season one's Frenchie—who competed under O.G. coach Christina Aguilera's tutelage—told Cosmopolitan in 2021 it was "always hysterical when the judges say, 'I don’t think that was a good song choice for you,' and I'm thinking, you picked that song.”

On the flip side, season 24 winner Huntley credited coach Niall Horan with helping him find his way, telling NBC Insider the One Direction alum "knows how to pick songs, I'll tell you that."

What sort of resources are available to help The Voice artists tend to their mental health?

Aspiring contestants are screened beforehand to see if they seem emotionally ready for the pressure that lies ahead, and then the show employs mental health professionals to help the artists both during and at the end of their journey.

“We had to start visiting to check on our well-being," season six alum Kat Perkins told Cosmopolitan of the counselors on staff. "The minute you are eliminated, you walk from that stage and into the psychiatrist’s office for a debriefing. They make sure that you talk about it. It’s very needed because you’ll never go through anything like it again. It’s traumatic and you’re not really emotionally set up to do something that big that quickly."

How do the chairs on The Voice really work?

The coaches are masters of their own domains, the big red chairs evolving over the years but always boasting the ability to turn around at the push of a button. In 2018 they received a sleek upgrade, including the addition of three more buttons—giving each coach the chance to block a fellow coach, once per round, from getting a chance at claiming the contestant behind the voice.

Not unlike a luxury car seat, in addition to an automobile-caliber aluminum frame and shiny paint job, each chair has self-adjusting heaters ("Me and Reba, we're the butt-warming kings," Snoop quipped to Access Hollywood) and dual cupholders (as requested by former coach Blake Shelton).

But, according to Perkins, the dramatic whoosh sound the chairs make when they turn around is added in post-production.

"You almost don’t notice it," she told Cosmo, "especially when you’re focusing and singing to the crowd that’s in the studio."

While congenial ribbing between coaches is part of the show's DNA, it was unclear at times over the course of the 16 seasons they were on The Voice together if Blake and Adam Levine were as exasperated with each other as they seemed.

"We are constantly at each other's throats, and sometimes we really do get mad at each other," Blake told The Tennessean in 2017. "We're those two guys you knew in high school where we have this bond that is unexplainable. It brings out the best and worst in both of us. It truly is an explosive relationship. And I know every trick to get under his skin."

Translation: "He's one of the best friends that I have, but I still want to kill him sometimes."

And even though they haven't competed against each other since 2019, Adam knows what the fans want.

"The Voice season 1 after party, at my house with dips--t @blakeshelton," the O.G. coach captioned a throwback pic ahead of his return to the show in February 2025 for season 27.

Meanwhile, subsequent crops of coaches were far less likely to tweet out each other's private phone numbers.

"You spend so much time together," Niall said during an NBC sit-down, "and I was hoping it wasn't going to be like this TV relationship where the cameras go around and we're like [feigning enthusiasm], 'Hey, Snoop Dogg!' I was always nervous about that, doing the show in the first place. I just didn't want it to be like a forced relationship, and it hasn't been that at all."

#795. NASA reveals a haunting skull hidden in Antarctica’s ice

Located in the Weddell Sea, east of the Antarctic Peninsula, Vega Island has a particularly haunting appearance when viewed from above. Its rocky and icy features resemble a grinning skull seen from the side, seemingly gazing toward nearby Devil Island. But behind this unusual sight is a more serious story about the changing condition of Antarctica's glaciers.

NASA satellite images show the island during the beginning of Antarctic autumn and during spring. The images were captured by the OLI (Operational Land Imager) aboard Landsat 9 on March 22, 2025, and October 10, 2026, respectively. (Clouds obscured the island in March 2026.)

Several natural landmarks create the skull's distinctive appearance. A nunatak, which is a rocky peak rising above the surrounding ice, resembles an empty eye socket. A lateral moraine, a ridge of material left along the side of a glacier, outlines the mouth. Meanwhile, Bahía del Diablo (Devil’s Bay) Glacier forms what looks like the skull's lower jaw.

The two satellite views also reveal a striking difference in snow coverage. In March 2025, snow blanketed the icy terrain, consistent with March being the wettest month in the region. By October 2026, however, extensive sections of the island were free of snow, leaving darker glacier ice exposed.

Glaciologist Mauri Pelto of Nichols College explained that unusually warm conditions during the winter of 2026, especially in June, contributed to the unusually large areas of exposed ice observed in October. According to Pelto, the exposed surfaces on Vega Island and neighboring islands suggest that relatively little fresh snow accumulated over the winter. Some of that snow was also lost through sublimation, when ice turns directly into water vapor, and through strong winds that swept snow away.

“The winter season was no treat for these glaciers.”

The lack of snow could have important consequences as Antarctica moves into its warmer months. Fresh snow reflects much of the sunlight that reaches it, while darker, exposed ice absorbs more solar energy. As daylight increases and temperatures rise, these darker surfaces are likely to warm more quickly, potentially speeding up glacier melting.

Even a modest amount of new snowfall could temporarily slow that process by covering the exposed ice.

“Even a thin cover of new snow from a spring storm would be helpful in the short run,” Pelto said.

Continued melting could also gradually transform the island's unsettling appearance. The same ice and rock formations that give Vega Island its skull shape are vulnerable to changes as the glaciers retreat.

“When entombed in snow and ice, the skull is preserved. But when exposed to melt, it weathers away, which will lead to a changing jawline and expanding eye socket.”

Scientists have been studying Vega Island's glaciers for decades, and satellite observations have played an important role in documenting their condition.

One of the earliest detailed surveys appeared in a 1982 study that used early Landsat satellite data, aerial photography, and topographic maps to examine the island's ice cover. Researchers identified four ice caps, along with rocky cliffs extending above the ice and glaciers flowing outward from the ice caps. Altogether, they documented 29 glaciers across Vega Island.

One of these, Devil's Bay Glacier, has been monitored in detail since the Antarctic summer of 1998-1999. Measurements collected over that period show an overall reduction in the glacier's mass.

The changes are not limited to Devil's Bay Glacier. Satellite observations spanning recent decades reveal that other glaciers on Vega Island have also lost ice, exposing increasing amounts of the underlying bedrock.

Long before satellites began monitoring its ice, Vega Island played an unexpected role in one of Antarctica's dramatic early exploration stories.

The Swedish Antarctic Expedition of 1901-1903 traveled to the region to investigate the geography, geology, climate, and wildlife of the eastern Antarctic Peninsula and surrounding areas. What began as a scientific mission turned into a desperate struggle for survival.

During the expedition, the explorers became separated into three groups, each forced to endure the Antarctic winter in a different location. Their situation became even more dangerous when pack ice destroyed their ship, leaving them stranded in one of the world's most unforgiving environments.

Despite the ordeal, Vega Island eventually became the setting for a moment of hope. In spring 1903, two of the separated groups reunited at a location later named Cape Well-met, near what now resembles the “forehead” of the island's giant skull.

Not long afterward, an Argentinean expedition arrived and rescued the survivors, bringing their extraordinary Antarctic ordeal to an end.

Today, Vega Island remains a place where dramatic natural formations, a remarkable history of exploration, and the effects of a changing climate come together. Its ghostly skull may be one of Antarctica's most unusual sights, but the gradual transformation of the ice that shapes it tells an even more important story.

NASA Earth Observatory images by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey.

CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners.

To build and sustain a base on the moon, NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8).

"We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said. "We're putting 1 million in prizes together to support the best ideas and recognize the teams behind them."

Isaacman made this announcement wearing his blue flight suit from the rocket garden at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center amidst the agency's MAX POWER air show event. Just the day before, he flew fighter jets in that suit and even jumped out of a plane, skydiving into the event. Soon after this announcement, he was flying another fighter plane above the crowd.

The audience for this announcement was filled with students of all ages. Some young children wearing costume spacesuits squeezed as close as they could to the front of the room while teenagers considering their futures listened intently. It was clear that Isaacman's presence and words were landing with this group.

But what moon base challenges does NASA want to see these students tackle? In short, all of them.

"The moon base will allow us to conduct groundbreaking science, test new technologies, and prepare again for where we inevitably go next, which is the red planet," he said. "But before any of that can happen, we have an awful lot of problems that need to be solved."

"We need ways to generate power through the long lunar night. We need to protect our astronauts from that incredibly harsh and dangerous and demanding environment on the surface. We need to move people and equipment around on the surface and support human life three days away from Earth," Isaacman said, illustrating just a few of the big issues that present with the concept of a moon base.

This challenge is open to high school and post-secondary students based in the U.S. For participating students, they will form teams that will work on an idea from one of six different technical topics related to creating and running a moon base. These six topics include power systems, habitats, communications, mobility, life support and astronaut safety.

This will be what Isaacman described as a "multi-phase competition that mirrors how ideas are developed actually in the aerospace industry."

"Teams will first submit concepts, then they're going to refine them, and finalists will have the opportunity to present their solutions directly to NASA leaders and stakeholders," he further explained.

"The prize money is great for sure, but the the real opportunity is to work on problems NASA is actively trying to solve right now, so students don't need to wait to graduation to contribute to that effort," Isaacman added.

Right now, NASA has a long road ahead of them before a moon base is actually built. In mid-2027, the agency is planning to launch its Artemis III mission which will see a crew of four astronauts practice rendezvous maneuvers with two different lunar landers. If all goes to plan, this will be followed by Artemis IV landing humans on the moon's surface for the first time since the final Apollo mission in 1972.

The agency is making these big steps forward to not just a crewed return to the moon, but a sustained, long-term return to the moon. However, knowing that a fully-fledged moon base is still firmly in the future, they are banking on the ingenuity, creativity and passion of

If you're a student or know a student interested in participating in this challenge, you can find more information on NASA's website here. Interested students can register until Jan. 25, 2027.

#793. Keira Knightley Reveals Which of Her Movies She’s Only Seen Once

Keira Knightley—who played Juliet in the 2003 film Love Actually—revealed she’s only seen the Christmas classic one time: “I think I’m the person that knows it the least of anybody.”

If you look for it, you'll find that Keira Knightley’s love for Love Actually isn’t, actually, all around.

After all, the 41-year-old—who played Juliet in the 2003 rom-com—revealed she’s only seen the film once.

“I have not watched Love Actually since the premiere, which was when I was 18,” she told Heart in a video shared Nov. 9. “So, I think I’m the person that knows it the least of anybody.”

And before you go asking her what could be worse than the total agony of being in love, just know there’s a high chance she’ll have no idea what you’re on about.

“I know that people have a particular look on their face and then they say things to me and I know that means they’re quoting Love Actually,” she explained, “but I don’t really know what it is. It means nothing to me.”

Plus, it doesn’t help that the Pirates of the Caribbean actress’ time on set was so short.

“It was a week when I was 17,” she noted. “So, I don’t remember it, really.”

Even so, she’s proud of the film’s legacy.

“I quite like that it has this life,” she added. “Such a big life out there.”

The Richard Curtis-directed Christmas classic follows a slew of interconnected love stories in London during the weeks leading up to the Dec. 25 holiday. And while some characters in the film get the s--t kicked out of them by love, Knightley’s Juliet finds herself in a love triangle with her husband Peter (Chiwetel Ejiofor) and his best friend Mark (Andrew Lincoln).

The situation comes to a head when Mark shows up on Christmas to profess his love using cue-cards. And while the scene has cemented itself as one of the most unforgettable rom-com moments in history, the Pride & Prejudice star previously revealed she and the film’s director worked hard to make sure the grand gesture didn’t seem "stalker-ish" for viewers.

“My memory is of Richard, who is now a very dear friend, of me doing the scene, and him going, ‘No, you’re looking at [Andrew] like he’s creepy,’" she told Variety in 2024. "And I’m like, ‘But it is quite creepy.’"

That’s why Knightley changed up her facial expression to try to improve the scene, recalling that she continued by “having to redo it to fix my face to make him seem not creepy.”

For more proof that Love Actually secrets really are all around, read on…

1. Love Actually opens with scenes of travelers hugging and kissing their nearest and dearest as they reunite at London's Heathrow Airport."This is my favorite bit in the film, in fact," writer/director Richard Curtis said in a director's commentary version of the film. "This footage was shot by a hidden camera, which was in Heathrow Airport for a whole week."And the movie's team really had to jet to get permission to use these clips of real-life passengers."Every time they saw something they really liked, then the runner would charge off and ask the people to sign a bit of paper, whether or not they were happy that it should be shown in the film," he continued. "I still think it'll be quite a surprise to the people who go to the cinema and see themselves."As for the inspiration behind the scene, it came from Curtis' personal experience."I got stuck in an airport in L.A. for an hour and a half waiting for a package, and I just saw all these people just all hugging and kissing," he added. "And you realize that behind normal people in the park and in the street, there's all these stories of love."

2. The first character fans meet in the 2003 movie is Bill Nighy's Billy Mack. He's a rock and roll star approaching his golden years who releases a holiday cover of Wet Wet Wet's "Love Is All Around," which secured the No. 1 spot in the U.K. for 15 weeks after the release of Curtis' 1994 film Four Weddings and a Funeral.While it can be hard to imagine anyone but Nighy playing the part, he wasn't initially in the running for the role. It wasn't until the actor stepped in to help with a table read that Curtis knew he was the one for the job."I had two famous guys in mind to play the aging rocker Billy Mack, and I couldn't decide who to ask," the filmmaker told The Guardian in 2013. "But at the read-through, Bill did it so perfectly he became a definite yes. I've never told anyone else who I wanted. I'll put it in my will."

3. Martin Freeman has also shared his casting story. In Love Actually, he portrays a man named John who meets a woman named Judy (Joanna Page) while they're stand-ins for a movie and filming a sex scene. They have great conversations, go out on a date and fall in love.At the time of casting, Curtis had fallen in love with the U.K. version of The Office, which Freeman starred on from 2001 to 2003."I got attached to Love Actually because on the back of The Office Richard Curtis wrote me a very nice and flattering letter that contained a piece of chocolate in it," The Hobbit star recalled to Vanity Fair in 2020. "It was like a wrapped chocolate presented to me saying, 'I love The Office. I love what you did in The Office. It was amazing.'"

4. Before Thomas Brodie-Sangster was cast as Sam—a British boy who loses his mom and turns to his stepdad Daniel (Liam Neeson) to help him navigate his crush on American schoolmate Joanna—Joe Alwyn tried out for the part."This local community center where I took fencing lessons, this brilliant U.K. casting director called Shaheen Baig, she came around and she saw me there," The Favourite alum and ex of Taylor Swift, shared on a 2018 episode of Live With Kelly and Ryan. "It meant that I got time off school to go to this audition, so I went to it."In fact, Alwyn said he went through several rounds of auditions and "a whole series of workshops" before the filmmakers decided to go with Brodie-Sangster."I didn't get it in the end, obviously," he added, "but I do remember meeting Hugh Grant and Richard Curtis and sitting down and reading some scenes."

5. Colin Firth played Jamie, a writer who leaves London for his French country home after learning his girlfriend cheated on him with his brother. There, Jamie meets Portuguese housekeeper Aurélia (Lúcia Moniz). And while they don't speak the same language, they understand the feelings they've formed for each other.Jamie returns to England for a family Christmas party only to turn back around and, after learning some Portugese, propose to Aurélia. As he leaves, his niece yells, "I hate Uncle Jamie." And apparently, the name was a playful jab at Curtis' brother."Richard only called colin firth's character 'jamie' so the kids could say 'I hate uncle jamie,'" his wife and script writer Emma Freud tweeted in 2015. "His brother is called jamie."6. As for Aurélia, Curtis shared in the director's commentary the name was a nod to a friend-slash-employee who looked after his and Emma's son.7. In one scene, Jamie types outside while Aurélia clears a cup that had been holding down his papers, resulting in the wind sweeping them into a lake. Curtis said they used a wind machine so loud the lines were dubbed.Aurélia dives in to retrieve the pages, and Jamie follows. However, Curtis said the lake was only 18 inches deep at the time of filming."They're kneeling now, pretending to swim, but actually crawling along the bottom, the poor things," he added in the commentary. "And Colin got stung by a sort of animal and his elbow swelled up to the size of three avocados the next day."

8. Martine McCutcheon played Natalie. Her character joins the staff of the newly elected prime minster David (Grant), and the two develop a crush on each other.Curtis knew McCutcheon was the one for the role right from the get-go."I wrote Martine McCutcheon's part for her, too," he told The Guardian. "I even called the character Martine, though I had to change it before the read-through so she didn't think she'd already got it."

9. One of Grant's most famous scenes is when he does a celebratory dance to The Pointer Sisters' song "Jump (For My Love)" after standing up to the U.S. president. However, the actor wasn't thrilled about having to bust out some moves."I think I saw it in the script," Grant said in 2022 for The Laughter & Secrets of Love Actually: 20 Years Later – A Diane Sawyer Special, "and I thought, 'Well I'll hate doing that.'"In fact, Curtis said Grant "kept saying no." Still, the Notting Hill star gave in eventually."He was grumpy," Curtis added in the special. "It was a contractual obligation, a bit of contractual obligation acting."As for his reaction to Grant's performance in that scene?"I’m thinking, ‘Oh, good he’s doing it,'" he recalled. "Two, that’s agonizingly embarrassing.”And Grant admits he was off with his lip-synching and dancing."I'm out of rhythm by the way," he told Diane Sawyer, "especially at the beginning when I wiggle my ass.”However, Grant is willing to take a bow for the scene's ending."It was my idea to have the secretary lady catch me," he noted in the special. "Genius!"

10. While it's clear Laura Linney's character Sarah had a crush on her co-worker Karl (Rodrigo Santoro), it wasn't as obvious to viewers that the costars were navigating their own heartaches off-screen."Hands down, I got the best kiss. Sorry!" the actress said on a 2019 episode of The Graham Norton Show, referencing Sarah and Karl's make-out session that ends when she receives a call about her brother Michael's mental health battle and leaves to be with him. "And it was sweet because we were both very brokenhearted when we made that movie. He had just been dumped, I had just been dumped."Linney recalled how she and Santoro were "slumped in the van" lamenting about their breakups while on their way to film the scene."I turned to him, and I said, 'Well all day long we get to make each other feel better,'" she remembered, "and I think there is a sweetness to the scene because of that. We were both very sad."

11. Fans certainly said "I do" to the scene where Keira Knightley's charater Juliet marries Chiwetel Ejiofor's Peter, especially the part where the couple walks down the aisle and are surprised by musicians popping up from the church pews to perform The Beatles' "All You Need Is Love."While the wedding is a joyful part of the film, the inspiration for it actually came from a day of mourning: Jim Henson's funeral, which Curtis called "the most moving thing" he's ever attended."At the end of it, Frank Oz was talking and he suddenly lifted up Kermit's puppet and started to sing this song called 'One Voice,'" he explained in the director's commentary. "And it turned out all the guys in the memorial service had brought their puppets with them, and they lifted them up. And when you turned around and looked backwards, there were 50 puppets all singing. And Big Bird walked down the aisle of St. Paul's Cathedral, and they all came forward and just this massive chorus of puppets all singing. It was an extraordinary thing. So, this was our little stab at that."

12. After the wedding, Juliet visits Peter's best friend Mark (Andrew Lincoln) to see if he captured any video footage of the wedding day. While she was under the impression he hated her, she learns (after popping in a VHS tape featuring footage of only her at the wedding) that he's actually been shielding his romantic feelings for her. In the scene, Juliet wears a hat. However, Knightley explained there was a reason for this fashion choice.

“I got the biggest zit of my life when we were shooting this scene,” the actress told Jimmy Fallon on a 2019 episode of The Tonight Show. “And this scene is the important one, isn’t it? It was like another head growing out of my head."While Knightley said the makeup and lighting departments tried to hide the pimple, it was no use."There was nothing they could do," the Pride & Prejudice star added, "so the hat went on."

13. Fast-forward to later in the movie, Mark shows up at Juliet and Peter's house and rings the door bell. When she answers, he instructs her to tell her husband it's carol singers. Mark then comes clean about his love for her through a series of cards, including one that says "To me, you are perfect." In fact, Lincoln actually wrote out the cards himself.

"It is my handwriting!" The Walking Dead actor told Entertainment Weekly in 2013. "It’s funny, because the art department did it, and then I said, 'Well, can I do it?' because I like to think that my handwriting is really good. Actually, it ended up with me having to sort of trace over the art department’s, so it is my handwriting, but with a sort of pencil stencil underneath."Juliet and Mark then part ways after she gives him a controversial kiss goodbye. In a 2017 sequel short for Red Nose Day, it's revealed that Juliet and Peter are still married and that Mark has tied the knot with supermodel Kate Moss, who was featured on one of his cards in the OG film.

And that wasn't the only notable memory from shooting the romantic moment. Knightley also recalled having to redo her reaction to his cue card reveal a few times so that the gesture seemed less "stalker-ish."

In a December 2024 interview withVariety, she detailed changing up her facial expression to try to improve the scene, saying she wound up “having to redo it to fix my face to make him seem not creepy.”

14. While there appears to be a bigger age gap between Knightley and Brodie-Sangster in the movie, they're only five years apart IRL. She was 17 when they made the film, and he was 12.

15. Brodie-Sangster really did learn how to play the drums for Love Actually, in which his character picks up the instrument to impress his crush Joanna (Olivia Olson) at their school's Christmas concert."I did learn to play the drums for it,” he told The Sunday Post in 2017. “My dad’s a drummer and he taught me in my grandad’s basement bashing away on his old kit and trying to play along to 'All I Want For Christmas [Is You].'”16. And yes, that really was Olson singing the Mariah Carey hit."Everyone thinks she is lip-synching, and she was 9 or 10 years old," screenwriter Freud said at the Montclair Film Festival in 2016, per the event's recap of her presentation, "but that was her.”17. What's more, the scene where Joanna gives Sam a peck on the cheek at London's Heathrow Airport before she flies back to America marked her first on- and off-screen kiss.

"I was really nervous because I kind of had a crush on Thomas back in the day," the actress told E! News in 2016, "and I was also worried because I was taller than him."The kiss clearly left an impression on both characters. In the 2017 Red Nose Day special, it's revealed that Sam reconnected with Joanna in New York and that they got engaged—with them flying back to London to ask Neeson's character Daniel for his blessing.

18. Another unforgettable scene is when the character Harry (played by the late Alan Rickman) is trying to buy a necklace for his secretary Mia (Heike Makatsch) without his wife Karen (Emma Thompson) knowing, but the jewelry salesman Rufus (Rowan Atkinson) is moving at a snail's pace.And apparently, the Mr. Bean star was in no rush to finish filming the scene.

20. One of the most heartbreaking parts of the movie is when Karen finds the necklace in Harry's coat pocket, thinks it for her and then unwraps a Joni Mitchell CD for Christmas instead—leading her to realize he bought the necklace for another woman.After she puts on a smile for their children's Christmas concert, Karen tells Harry she knows what's going on. And while fans wondered if the couple remained married, Freud solved this mystery. "They stay together," she tweeted in 2015, "but home isn't as happy as it once was."And Freud says Harry's relationship with Mia went beyond the necklace."DEFINITELY had an affair," she wrote, "i begged richard just to make it a flirtation, but no. the whole way."

21. With several other beloved rom-coms under his belt—including Four Weddings and a Funeral, Notting Hill and Bridget Jones's Diary—Curtis resurfaced a scene he'd cut in a previous film for Love Actually.The scene stars a man named Colin (Kris Marshall), who is serving hors d'oeuvres at a wedding. In a failed attempt to flirt, he strikes up a conversation with a woman and tells her how bad the food is—except it turns out the woman is the caterer."This highly amusing scene coming up now about catering with this girl is a re-working of a highly amusing scene about catering, which bore remarkable resemblance down to the last line which was originally in Four Weddings and a Funeral," Grant, who appeared in both films, revealed while doing the director's commentary with Curtis, "which was one of my audition scenes, but which got cut from the final film."In fact, Curtis admitted he forgot to change the name from Charles in Four Weddings and a Funeral to Colin in Love Actually in a line of the re-worked script.22. Fed up with searching for love in the U.K., Colin decides to go to America and try his luck there. He flies to Wisconsin, where he meets a group of women at a bar, including one named Jeannie played by January Jones."January jones wrote half of her lines," Freud revealed in a tweet. "She was sooooo funny when we filmed that scene."

23. While there were several familiar faces in Love Actually, Freud revealed her and Curtis' kids also made a few cameos."THAT IS SCARLETT CURTIS THERE ON THE RIGHT," she tweeted about her daughter, who was dressed as one of the lobsters in the school's Nativity play (yes, you read that right). "NOT EVEN JOKING."In addition, she noted the boy with the crown and Spider-Man face-paint in the Christmas play is their son Jake, with her writing, "I gave birth to him."24. Looking back at the film two decades later, Curtis admits there are aspects of the film he wishes he could change."The lack of diversity makes me feel uncomfortable and a bit stupid," he admitted in the Diane Sawyer special. "I think there are three plots that have bosses and people who work for them."The director has also expressed regret over the film's comments about Natalie's weight.“I think I was behind, you know, behind the curve, and those jokes aren’t any longer funny," he told The Hollywood Reporter in 2023, "so I don’t feel I was malicious at the time, but I think I was unobservant and not as, you know, as clever as I should have been.”

25. While Love Actually features 10 different storylines, Curtis said he originally had more.

"At first, we had 14 different love stories, but the result was too long, so four ended up going, including two we'd actually shot," he told The Guardian. "One was based on a poster in Alan Rickman's office of two women in Africa. The camera actually went into the poster and heard them talking about their daughters' love lives. Another involved Emma Thompson's son getting into trouble at school and the camera following the harsh headmistress home."In the since-released deleted scenes, the headmistress can be seen heading home to take care of her partner Geraldine, who is dealing with an illness and later dies. Another deleted scene shows Sarah talking about family Christmas memories with her brother Michael. They ask each other how they're doing now. While Sarah says "everything's great," Michael gets real with her about his mental health struggles and says, "I'm in hell."Even though Curtis decreased the number of storylines, he admitted stringing the remaining ones together was no easy feat.

"Although all the strands come together in the airport at the end, it still felt like making 10 separate films," he told The Guardian. "It was a massively difficult edit. The order I originally wrote it in didn't work at all, so we had to reorder it completely. It was a bizarre four-month game of 3D chess."

#792. A tiny squeeze dramatically changes the magnetism of exotic materials

Scientists at the Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory have discovered that applying a small amount of pressure can dramatically alter the magnetic properties of a promising new class of materials called altermagnets. Using neutron experiments, the researchers uncovered how a simple mechanical squeeze can change the way these materials behave, offering a potential new approach to controlling magnetism.

The results, reported in two consecutive studies published in Physical Review X and Advanced Materials, show that mechanical strain can influence both magnetic structures and the movement of electrons. This ability could provide a straightforward way to control materials being investigated for advanced electronic technologies.

Why Altermagnets Matter for Future Electronics

One particularly promising application involves spintronics, short for spin electronics. Unlike conventional electronics, which processes and stores information using the electrical charge of electrons, spintronics also takes advantage of a property known as electron spin.

If scientists can identify and develop suitable materials, including altermagnets, this approach could lead to major advances in technologies ranging from wireless communication to quantum computing.

"By controlling the magnetic domains, we can directly influence the transport behavior, and that opens the door to exploring these materials for spintronic technologies," said Pengcheng Dai of Rice University, a former neutron scientist at ORNL.

A Simple Squeeze Reveals Surprising Magnetic Changes

To investigate how pressure affects these materials, the ORNL team placed tiny crystals of manganese telluride and iron sulfide between a pair of titanium plates and gently compressed them.

Using neutron diffraction at ORNL's Spallation Neutron Source, the scientists examined what happened to the magnetic structures inside the crystals. They found that the applied pressure changed the relative populations of magnetic domains, which are regions within a material that have particular magnetic arrangements. The strain also altered an electrical phenomenon called the anomalous Hall effect, providing evidence that the mechanical squeeze influenced the materials' electrical behavior.

"What's exciting is that one creative experimental idea -- a small mechanical squeeze between two plates -- can reveal entirely new magnetic behavior and push the field forward, and neutron scattering plays such a critical role, revealing the underlying change in magnetism," said Feng Ye, an ORNL neutron scientist and co-author on both linked publications.

The findings highlight how a relatively simple experiment can uncover new ways to manipulate magnetic materials, potentially helping researchers develop the building blocks for future spintronic devices.

ORNL's Spallation Neutron Source is a DOE Office of Science user facility.

#791. How Hip-Hop Changed the Billboard Charts: From ‘Rapper’s Delight’ to Today | Billboard News

From Sugarhill Gang’s “Rapper’s Delight” breaking into the Hot 100 to chart milestones from Ms. Lauryn Hill, Eminem, Outkast, Drake and Kendrick Lamar, look back at the moments that helped hip-hop reshape music and culture.

From block parties in the Bronx to the top of the Billboard charts, hip-hop has spent decades breaking records, crossing boundaries, and changing the sound of popular music. In celebration of National Hip-Hop History Month, we’re looking back at the groundbreaking moments that shaped the genre’s rise, the artists who rewrote the record books, and the milestones that changed music forever. This is Billboard News, presented by Lexus. Let’s rewind to 1980, when the Sugarhill Gang’s “Rapper’s Delight” became the first hip-hop single to break into the top 40 of the Billboard Hot 100, reaching No. 36. By 1986, Run-D.M.C. was breaking barriers with Aerosmith on “Walk This Way,” bringing hip-hop to an even wider audience. And in 1989, Billboard launched its first dedicated rap chart, giving the growing genre a new platform to measure its success. By the ’90s, hip-hop wasn’t just climbing the charts, it was taking over. In 1998, Lauryn Hill made history when The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, setting a new first-week sales record for a female artist at the time. Just a few years later, Eminem’s The Marshall Mathers LP delivered one of the biggest debut weeks in hip-hop history, while Outkast’s “Hey Ya!” spent nine weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
